results.claim: Swish containment is exactly a multiplicity-respecting directed-cycle problem.
results.proof_sketch: Fix one allowed transformation for each card in a proposed Swish and direct its arc from hoop to ball. Every used grid point then has indegree and outdegree one, so every nonempty connected component is a directed simple cycle; the physical cards of any one component are themselves a Swish. Conversely, distinct physical cards realizing a directed simple cycle put exactly one hoop and one ball at each cycle vertex. Thus a collection contains a Swish exactly when some directed simple cycle can be realized without using any transformation type more often than the number of selected physical copies of that type.

results.claim: The transformation action gives four position orbits, eight internal card types, and twenty-eight cross-orbit types in fourteen reversal pairs.
results.proof_sketch: Let K be the Klein four group generated by horizontal and vertical reflection. Its position orbits are A={(1,1),(1,3),(4,1),(4,3)}, B={(1,2),(4,2)}, C={(2,1),(2,3),(3,1),(3,3)}, and D={(2,2),(3,2)}. A and C are free K-orbits; B and D have the same order-two stabilizer. Ordered distinct pairs internal to A and C therefore give three types each, while B and D give one each. For an unordered pair of position orbits, the number of types in either direction is |K/(H_iH_j)|; in the order AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD these numbers are 2,4,2,2,2,2. They sum to fourteen in each chosen direction, and reversing every ordered pair bijects the two directions. Hence there are 8+28=36 types.

results.claim: A no-swish collection contains at most 20 distinct transformation types, and this is sharp.
results.proof_sketch: Both members of any cross-orbit reversal pair realize opposite arcs, hence a two-cycle, so at most one of each of the fourteen pairs can occur. On either free four-position orbit, the three internal types are the three nonidentity translations of K and one copy of each realizes a directed triangle, so at most two occur. Each two-position orbit has only its sole internal type. Thus the support bound is 14+2+1+2+1=20. Equality is attained by ordering A<B<C<D, taking all fourteen forward cross types, and taking one card of each internal type represented by (1,1)→(1,3), (1,1)→(4,1), (1,2)→(4,2), (2,1)→(2,3), (2,1)→(3,1), and (2,2)→(3,2). Cross arcs strictly increase orbit rank, and the internal choices contain no cycle.

results.claim: Every 60-card once-or-twice model has a 28-card no-swish subset; unless all eight internal types are doubled, it has a 29-card no-swish subset.
results.proof_sketch: Assume all 36 types occur once or twice, so exactly 24 are doubled. Let M0 be the total physical multiplicity of the eight internal types. Across the 24 total orders of A,B,C,D, each physical cross card points forward in exactly 12 orders. Hence some order has at least ceil((60−M0)/2) forward cross cards. Add one card of each of the six internal types in the sharp-support construction. No cycle can contain a cross arc because orbit rank strictly increases, and the internal part is cycle-free. Since M0≤16, this always gives at least 22+6=28 cards. If an internal type is not doubled, then M0≤15, so it gives at least 23+6=29; extras may be discarded.

results.claim: If a once-or-twice model has maximum no-swish size 28, then all eight internal types are doubled and the cross-card multiplicities are directionally balanced between every pair of position orbits.
results.proof_sketch: The preceding construction forces all internal types to be doubled. They then contribute 16 cards, leaving 44 cross cards. For distinct orbits i,j, let W_ij be the total physical multiplicity of types directed i→j. If F(pi) is the number of cross cards forward in an orbit order pi, then the average of F over all 24 orders is 22. If W_ij differs from W_ji, put i,j adjacently and swap them. No other relative order changes, while F changes by W_ji−W_ij. Thus the integer values F are nonconstant while averaging 22, so some F is at least 23. Its forward cards plus the six safe internal cards form a 29-card no-swish subset, a contradiction. Therefore W_ij=W_ji for all six unordered orbit pairs.

results.claim: When all eight internal types are doubled, any no-swish subset contains at most six internal cards.
results.proof_sketch: Every internal type is invariant under reversal: applying the relevant order-two symmetry exchanges its endpoints. Two physical copies of one internal type can therefore realize opposite arcs and form a two-card Swish, so at most one copy of each internal type may be selected. On A and C, selecting all three internal types realizes a directed triangle, so each contributes at most two cards. B and D each have one internal type and contribute at most one. The total internal contribution is at most 2+1+2+1=6.

results.claim: For a fixed unordered orbit pair with k reversal pairs and d doubled types in each direction, a no-swish subset contains at most k+d cards between those two orbits.
results.proof_sketch: Write the position orbits as K/H_i and K/H_j. Cross types in either direction are labeled by delta in K/(H_iH_j); reversal preserves the label because every element of K has order two. Positive selections in both directions with the same label make a two-cycle. If distinct labels delta and epsilon are each selected twice in opposite directions, choose representatives and a starting point x=gH_i. Alternating the two types gives x=gH_i→gdelta H_j→gdeltaepsilon H_i→gepsilon H_j→gH_i. Since delta and epsilon are distinct modulo H_iH_j, these are four distinct vertices, so the four cards form a Swish. Consequently, among a no-swish selection, at most one direction can supply any second-copy bonuses. The reverse-pair two-cycles allow at most k first copies total, and directional balance leaves only d doubled types in whichever direction supplies bonuses. Hence the local cap is k+d.

results.claim: Under the once-or-twice model, maximum no-swish size is exactly 28 if and only if all eight internal types are doubled and W_ij=W_ji for every unordered position-orbit pair.
results.proof_sketch: Necessity was proved above. For sufficiency, all eight internal types use eight of the 24 duplications, so sixteen doubled cross types remain. For the six unordered orbit pairs let k_ij be the number of reversal pairs and let d_ij be the number of doubled types in either direction; balance makes this well-defined. Then sum k_ij=14 and 2 sum d_ij=16, so sum d_ij=8. The local obstruction bounds all selected cross cards by sum(k_ij+d_ij)=22, while the internal obstruction bounds internal cards by six. Thus every no-swish subset has size at most 28. The averaging construction gives one of size at least 28, so the maximum is exactly 28. If either condition fails, the earlier constructions give 29, proving the equivalence.

results.claim: The sealed source omits information essential to deciding the exact commercial-deck target, even though the once-or-twice abstract model now has an exact criterion.
results.proof_sketch: The source states only that the commercial deck has 60 cards and 36 symmetry types, with some equivalent cards appearing twice; it gives neither the internal duplication flags nor the six directional totals. This omission is outcome-relevant even within the once-or-twice model. Deck X doubles all eight internal types and both directions of eight reversal pairs; it is balanced and therefore has maximum 28. Fixing A<B<C<D, Deck Y doubles all fourteen backward cross types, nine forward cross types, and one internal type. Selecting both copies of those nine forward types, one copy of each other forward type, and the six safe internal cards gives 18+5+6=29 no-swish cards. Both decks contain all 36 types, have exactly 24 doubled types and 60 cards, and satisfy the supplied aggregates, but their target answers differ.

final_writeup:
Transform each selected physical card and direct an arc from its hoop to its ball. A collection contains a Swish exactly when distinct physical cards from it can realize a directed simple cycle. A Swish has indegree and outdegree one at every used point, so each component is such a cycle; conversely a directed cycle places exactly one hoop and one ball at each of its vertices. This formulation keeps the number of available physical copies explicit.

Let K be the Klein four transformation group. The twelve grid positions split into A={(1,1),(1,3),(4,1),(4,3)}, B={(1,2),(4,2)}, C={(2,1),(2,3),(3,1),(3,3)}, and D={(2,2),(3,2)}. A and C are free K-orbits, while B and D have an order-two stabilizer. There are 3,1,3,1 internal types on A,B,C,D. For AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD there are respectively 2,4,2,2,2,2 types in either direction, giving fourteen cross-orbit reversal pairs and 36 total types.

This immediately gives the audited sharp support bound. A no-swish collection uses at most one type from every cross reversal pair, and on A or C it uses at most two of the three internal types because all three realize a triangle. Thus it has at most 14+2+1+2+1=20 distinct types. Equality is obtained by choosing all cross types forward in an order of A,B,C,D and the six internal representatives

(1,1)→(1,3), (1,1)→(4,1), (1,2)→(4,2),
(2,1)→(2,3), (2,1)→(3,1), (2,2)→(3,2).

Now impose the explicit once-or-twice model: all 36 types occur, each with multiplicity one or two. Exactly 24 types are doubled. If the eight internal types have total multiplicity M0, average the number of physical cross cards pointing forward over the 24 orders of A,B,C,D. Every cross card is forward in twelve orders, so some order has at least ceil((60−M0)/2) forward cards. Adding one copy of each of the six safe internal types remains cycle-free: cross arcs strictly raise orbit rank, and the internal part has no cycle. This always constructs 28 cards. If M0≤15, it constructs at least 29. Hence a deck with maximum 28 must double every internal type.

If all internal types are doubled, there are 44 cross cards and the average forward count is 22. Write W_ij for the physical multiplicity directed from orbit i to orbit j. If W_ij≠W_ji, place i,j adjacently in an orbit order and swap them. Only their contribution changes, so the forward counts are nonconstant integers averaging 22. Some order has at least 23 forward cards, and the six safe internal cards again yield 29. Directional balance W_ij=W_ji for all six pairs is therefore necessary.

The obstruction lens makes this condition sufficient as well. First, a doubled internal type cannot contribute both copies: they can be transformed into opposite arcs and form a two-cycle. The three internal types on A or C form a triangle, so at most 2+1+2+1=6 internal cards can occur.

For the cross cards, fix two position orbits K/H_i and K/H_j. Their k types in either direction are labeled by K/(H_iH_j). Equal labels in opposite directions are reverse types and form a two-cycle with one copy each. Distinct labels delta,epsilon selected twice in opposite directions form the four-cycle

gH_i→gdelta H_j→gdeltaepsilon H_i→gepsilon H_j→gH_i.

Thus a no-swish subset cannot take second-copy bonuses in both directions between the same two orbits. Reverse-pair obstructions allow at most k first copies, and if d types are doubled in each direction, at most d second copies can be taken. The local cap is k+d.

Under directional balance, sixteen cross types are doubled, so if d_ij is the common doubled-type count in the two directions, sum d_ij=8. Since the six values k_ij sum to fourteen, at most 14+8=22 cross cards and six internal cards can be selected. The lower construction already supplies 28. Therefore, in the once-or-twice model, the maximum no-swish size is exactly 28 if and only if all eight internal types are doubled and every W_ij is balanced; otherwise a 29-card no-swish subset exists.

This does not settle the named commercial deck from the sealed source, because the source supplies neither the internal duplication flags nor the directional totals. The omission is decisive. A compatible Deck X doubles all internal types and both directions of eight reversal pairs, so the criterion gives maximum 28. A compatible Deck Y doubles all fourteen backward types, nine forward types, and one internal type; its nine doubled forward types, five other forward types, and six safe internal cards give 18+5+6=29 no-swish cards. Both have 60 cards, all 36 types, and exactly 24 doubled types.

The result is therefore partial for the requested commercial-deck target but exact for the stated once-or-twice abstraction. Deciding the actual target still requires enough of the commercial multiplicity data to test the criterion; the sealed source contains no such data.
